title: The Forgotten Library
intro: You wake up on a cold wooden floor. Dusty shelves tower around you and the only exit is a heavy oak door with a four-digit keypad. Somewhere in this library is the way out.

desk.name: writing desk
desk.description: An old oak writing desk. A leather journal and a brass magnifying glass lie on top of it.

journal.name: leather journal
journal.description: The librarian's journal. One page reads: 'Three red books guard my drawer - read them left to right.' Another page reads: 'The clock stopped the night I left. Its face remembers the end of the way out.'

magnifying_glass.name: magnifying glass
magnifying_glass.description: A brass magnifying glass. Useful for reading very small text.

bookshelf.name: bookshelf
bookshelf.description: A tall bookshelf full of grey, dusty books. Three bright red books stand out on the middle shelf.

red_books.name: three red books
red_books.description: Each red book has a single number handwritten on its first page. From left to right they read: 4, 7, 2.

drawer.name: locked drawer
drawer.description: A drawer built into the side of the desk, secured with a three-digit combination lock.
drawer.opened_description: The drawer is open and empty now.

lock.success_text: The lock clicks and the drawer slides open. Inside are a small brass key and a torn note.

brass_key.name: brass key
brass_key.description: A small brass key with an ornate handle. It looks like it belongs to a picture frame lock.

torn_note.name: torn note
torn_note.description: The note says: 'The beginning of the way out hides behind my portrait.'

painting.name: portrait
painting.description: A portrait of a stern old librarian. The frame is hinged to the wall and has a tiny brass keyhole.
painting.opened_description: The portrait hangs open on its hinges. The digits 5 and 8 are scratched into the wall behind it.

lock.success_text: The brass key turns and the portrait swings open like a door. Scratched into the stone behind it are the digits 5 and 8.

clock.name: grandfather clock
clock.description: A tall grandfather clock, stopped long ago. Something is engraved on its face but the letters are far too small to read with the naked eye.

inspect_with.success_text: Through the magnifying glass you read the tiny engraving on the clock face: 'the end is 1 then 3'.

door.name: oak door
door.description: A heavy oak door with a four-digit keypad. It is the only way out.
door.opened_description: The oak door stands wide open. Fresh air flows in.

lock.success_text: The keypad flashes green. With a heavy clunk the oak door swings open. You have escaped the Forgotten Library!

clues.journal_hints: Journal: the three red books hold the drawer code (read left to right); the stopped clock holds the end of the exit code.
clues.note_hint: The torn note says the beginning of the exit code is behind the portrait.

hints.text: The bookshelf and the desk both deserve a closer look.
Something you found in the drawer might fit a very small keyhole.
Tiny engravings need a tool to read.
Put the beginning and the end of the code together and try the keypad.
